subject: Agriculture
title: Post-War Food Insecurity
description: Learn Post-War Food Insecurity in one minute.

hook.text: After World War II, much of Asia and Africa couldn't feed its growing populations. Hunger was everywhere.

buildup.text: India relied on US food aid—millions of tons of surplus wheat shipped under PL-480 agreements.

discovery.text: Dependence on food imports left nations vulnerable. A delayed shipment meant starvation.

twist.text: President Johnson withheld food shipments to pressure India on policy. Food aid became a political weapon.

climax.text: India's humiliation fueled a national commitment to grow its own food—at any cost. The stage was set.

punchline.text: Hunger drove dependence. Dependence drove revolution.

quiz.question: Why did India's dependence on US food aid become problematic?
options: The US withheld shipments as political leverage

details.summary: The aftermath of World War II left much of Europe and Asia facing severe food shortages due to destroyed farmland, disrupted supply chains, and displaced populations. This topic covers the global hunger crisis of the late 1940s and how it motivated international agricultural development efforts.
details.whyItMatters: Post-war food insecurity created the international institutions and political will that funded Green Revolution research. The Rockefeller and Ford Foundations, FAO, and CGIAR system all emerged from this era of global hunger.
takeaways: World War II destroyed farmland and infrastructure across Europe, Asia, and North Africa
Post-war food shortages affected hundreds of millions and risked political instability
International development agencies were created specifically to address global hunger

faq.question: How severe was the food crisis after World War II?
faq.answer: Europe's agricultural output had fallen 25-50% from pre-war levels. Millions of displaced people had no access to farmland. Japan's food production collapsed. India, already weakened by the Bengal Famine, faced chronic shortages. The U.S. became the world's primary food donor through emergency aid.

faq.question: How did post-war hunger lead to the Green Revolution?
faq.answer: The Rockefeller Foundation began funding agricultural research in Mexico in 1943 to increase food production in developing countries. The FAO was founded in 1945 to address global hunger.
